texts.preamble: Murthuja Ali Alias Damar vs The State Of Telengana on 4 July, 2023 Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K.Lakshman, P.Sree Sudha Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman And Hon'Ble Smt. Justice P. Sree Sudha Writ Petition No.40604 Of 2022 Order:
texts.facts: 2. This writ petition is filed to issue a writ of Habeas Corpus declaring the order of detention dated 15.10.2022 passed by respondent No.2 and the consequential confirmation order by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.2247, dated 01.12.2022 as illegal and to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the same and for a consequential direction to release the detenu, Mr. Murthuja Ali @ Damar, S/o Babar Ali. 3. Respondent No.2 passed the detention order dated 15.10.2022 under the provisions of Section - 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities KL,J & PSS,J Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Act No.1 of 1986) (for short 'Act No.1 of 1986'), under the category of 'Goonda' as defined under Section - 2 (g) of the Act. 4. The wife of the detenu, Mrs. Fiza Ali, filed the writ affidavit. The aforesaid detention order was passed by respondent No.2 relying on the following four (04) crimes; Crime No. Offences Allegations Remarks levelled 428/2022 of Sections - 392 Snatching two Bail applications filed by KPHB P.S. & 307 of IPC gold pustelathadu the detenu were dismissed. (PRC No.157/2022) 467/2022 of Section - 392 Snatching gold Bail petition not yet Chandanagar P.S. of IPC pusthalathadu moved. (C.C. No.6156 of 2022 is pending) 709/2022 of -do- Snatching gold Bail petition not yet Murthuja Ali Alias Damar vs The State Of Telengana on 4 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126857507/ 1 Miyapur P.S. chain moved. (CC 7060 of 2022 is pending) 321/2022 of Section - 393 Tried to snatch Bail petition not yet Bachupally P.S. of IPC gold chain moved. (CC 5977 of 202 is pending) 5. In the detention order, there is reference with regard to the involvement of the detenu in seventy five (75) property offences under different Police Stations of the States of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana during the years from KL,J & PSS,J 2005 to 2015. In the year 2016 also, detention order was issued by Hyderabad Police Commissionerate and he was detained in Central Prison at Cherlapally. After serving detention period, he was released from the Jail in July, 2021. Despite the same, he did not mend his attitude and again involved in the aforesaid four (04) cases apart from Crime No.589 of 2022 of Medipally Police Station registered for the offence punishable under Section - 379 of IPC with regard to theft of parked motorcycle. After having come to the subjective satisfaction only, the detaining authority passed the impugned detention order. 6. As per the contents of the order of detention and the counter affidavit filed by respondent No.2, the grounds for passing the order of detention are that the detenu has been repeatedly indulging in the acts of 'goondaism' by committing property offences i.e., chain snatchings in an organized way and creating terror and a feeling of insecurity among the public especially women folks which disturbs peace and tranquility in the ear and acted in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order. 7. Perusal of the record would reveal that the detenu committed the aforesaid four (04) crimes apart from Crime No.589 of 2022 of Medipally Police Station during the year 2022. Earlier, the detenu also KL,J & PSS,J involved in 75 property offences under different police station limits in the aforementioned States. According to the respondent authorities, earlier also P.D. Act was imposed on the detenu and he was sent to Central Prison, Cherlapally. After his release in the month of July, 2021, there was no change in his attitude and continues in commission of similar offences. Therefore, to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences which would disturb the public order, respondent No.2 issued the impugned detention order dated 15.10.2022. The same was confirmed by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.2247, dated 01.12.2022. As discussed above, though the detaining authority referred to about the involvement of the detenu in 75 crimes during the years 2005 to 2015 and Crime No.589 of 2022, he has relied upon the four (04) crimes/cases mentioned in the above said table and issued the impugned detention order. All the said four crimes are relating to chain snatchings within the jurisdiction of respondent No.2. 11.
texts.arguments: 8. Mr. Rachakonda Ramakrishna, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that though the aforesaid four (04) crimes were referred and relied on by the detaining authority for passing order of detention, the same can be dealt with by ordinary law by the competent Criminal Courts instead of passing impugned detention order. He would further submit that the offences alleged to have committed by the detenu come under the ambit of law and order and the same are against particular individual. Further, the crimes were registered against the detenu based on confessions. The detaining authority passed the order of detention on flimsy grounds without any basis in a mechanical manner. There are no material to substantiate and justify for treating the detenu as KL,J Murthuja Ali Alias Damar vs The State Of Telengana on 4 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126857507/ 2 & PSS,J 'Goonda'. Therefore, he sought to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned detention order and the consequential confirmation order. 9. On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General would submit that the allegations levelled against the detenu are serious in nature, as he is a 'habitual offender' in many chain snatching cases and other serious offences in various States, the details of which are mentioned in the counter affidavit. In Crime No.428 of 2022 of KPHB Police Station, the detenu while committing the offence of chain snatching made an attempt to kill the victim. There is no error in it. i) Learned Special Government Pleader placed reliance on the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vijay Kumar v. KL,J & PSS,J Union of India1 and Smt. K. Aruna Kumari v. Government of Andhra Pradesh2. 10. Section - 2 (g) of the Act No.1 of Act, 1986 defines "Goonda", which means a person, who either by himself or as a member of or leader of a gang, habitually . (1988) 1 SCC 296 KL,J & PSS,J commits, or attempts to commit or abets the commission of offences punishable under Chapter XVI or Chapter XVII or Chapter XXII of the IPC. 12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration3 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society. The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing. 13. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar4, the Apex Court held as under: Murthuja Ali Alias Damar vs The State Of Telengana on 4 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126857507/ 3 "...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder. When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder. They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order. Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions. Other examples can be imagined. A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are. It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order". In Mallada K. Sri Ram v. The State of Telangana5, the Apex Court considering the fact that only two (02) crimes were registered against the detenu and he was granted bail on imposition of certain conditions, and there was no disturbance to the public order, [LEAKAGE_MASK] the detention order. 15. In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar6, a three Judge Bench of the Apex Court had an occasion to deal with the expression 'habitually' and held that the expression 'habitually' would mean . Aruna Kumari2, the Apex Court held that this Court cannot examine probative value of evidence available to the detaining authority. Therefore, the facts of the KL,J & PSS,J present case are different to the facts of the case in Mallada K. Sri Ram5, wherein only two (02) crimes were registered against the detenu for the offences punishable under Sections - 420, 468, 471 and 506 read with 120B of IPC and, therefore, the Apex Court considering the same and that the detenu was granted bail on imposition of certain conditions, and there was no disturbance to the public order, [LEAKAGE_MASK] the detention order. 21.
